books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Thomas Nast, “The Union as It Was — The Lost Cause, Worse than Slavery,” Harper’s Weekly, October 24, 1874

stimulus.text: Thomas Nast’s cartoon “The Union as It Was — The Lost Cause, Worse than Slavery,” Harper’s Weekly, October 24, 1874. A man marked “White League,” a rifle on his back, shakes hands with a hooded Klansman marked “K.K.” over a shield. Above them an eagle carries the words “The Union as It Was” and “This Is a White Man’s Government.” Inside the shield, a Black mother and father crouch over their baby in grief, while behind them a freedman hangs from a tree and a schoolhouse burns. A child’s primer lies dropped on the ground.
stimulus.source_note: Thomas Nast, “The Union as It Was — The Lost Cause, Worse than Slavery,” Harper’s Weekly, October 24, 1874, p. 878 (Library of Congress, LCCN2001696840). Public domain. Image viewed before writing; details described from the image itself.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The burning schoolhouse and the dropped primer in the cartoon most directly show that the attackers were targeting

options.text: the federal troops stationed in Southern cities.
options.misconception: No soldiers appear in the cartoon; the victims are a Black family.

options.text: Black education and the chance to rise through learning.
the Republican Party’s campaign funds in the South.
options.misconception: The burning building is labeled “School House,” not a party office.

options.text: the railroads that carried freedpeople out of the South.
options.misconception: Background: no railroad appears in the cartoon, and the Exoduster migration came later, in 1879.

rationales.A: No soldiers appear in the cartoon; the victims are a Black family.
rationales.B: The schoolhouse burns while a child’s alphabet primer lies dropped in the dirt. Nast shows the attackers striking at Black schooling itself, the path freed families hoped would lift their children.
rationales.C: The burning building is labeled “School House,” not a party office.
rationales.D: Background: no railroad appears in the cartoon, and the Exoduster migration came later, in 1879.
rationales.general:
1. Nast labels the burning building plainly: “School House.”
2. The primer on the ground is a child’s first book, dropped in flight.
3. Schools were where freed families put their hopes for the next generation.
4. Burning a school says the attackers feared Black learning as much as Black voting.
Remember: in a cartoon, a small labeled object often carries the whole argument.
